real_conflicts: Blurring the typography (Visual Concept/Color proposals) destroys the structural anchor of the composition. The title 'THE WEIGHT OF AIR' must remain sharp to provide a rigid grid against which the fluid, blurred body can struggle. If both are blurred, the image becomes a muddy, illegible wash with no spatial tension.

Centering the title (Current State) creates a static, symmetrical layout that feels like a generic event card. The figure's dynamic, diagonal energy is neutralized by the passive, centered text, resulting in a lack of visual conflict.
accepted: Disrupting the alignment by shifting the title text off-center to create asymmetry (My original proposal). This creates the necessary spatial tension and prevents the layout from feeling like a standard template.
Using a heavy, directional blur on the figure to suggest speed and instability (My original proposal). This is essential to convey the 'movement' and 'collapse' requested in the brief.
concession: I concede that the figure's current 'stick figure' quality is too generic. I accept the need to introduce 'fragmentation' or 'glitch' elements to the body's form to suggest the 'tension' and 'breaking apart' mentioned in the brief, rather than just a smooth speed blur.
compromise: We will shift the title 'THE WEIGHT OF AIR' to the left to create an asymmetrical, dynamic balance. The text will remain sharp and high-contrast (white) to act as a solid structural wall. The figure will be modified to include fragmentation/glitch effects but will aggressively overlap and obscure parts of the text, creating a physical conflict between the 'weight' of the words and the 'air' of the body.
nonnegotiable: The typography must remain sharp and legible to serve as the structural anchor of the composition.
